title: Chapter 56: Sandu: The Three Poisons 1
content:
Chapter 56

Sandu: The Three Poisons 1

He never did catch the name of that song.

A hot rush of blood surged into his face, fever flaring so fiercely through his skull and joints that it set them screaming with pain, accompanied by a relentless, high-pitched ringing in his ears.

When he finally opened his eyes again, Wei Wuxian was greeted not by the pitch-black ceiling of an underground cavern, nor by the pale, striking face of Lan Wangji. Instead, he stared up at a wooden board adorned with a ridiculous string of kissing stick figures—the doodle he’d scribbled above his own bed back in Lotus Pier.

Wei Wuxian was sprawled across his wooden cot. Nearby, head bowed over a book, sat Jiang Yanli. The moment she saw him stir, her delicate brows arched in delight. Dropping the book, she called out, "A-Xian!"

"Shijie!" Wei Wuxian croaked.

He dragged himself upright with no small effort. The fever had broken, but his limbs felt like damp noodles and his throat was bone-dry. "I'm back? When did I get out of that cave? Did Uncle Jiang bring a rescue team? Where's Lan Zhan? Where's Jiang Cheng?"

The wooden door swung open with a bang. Jiang Cheng strolled in, hauling a white porcelain crock in one hand. "Quit your hollering!" he snapped.

Turning to Jiang Yanli, his tone softened immediately. "Jie, I brought the soup you made."

Jiang Yanli took the crock, ladling its contents into a bowl.

Wei Wuxian waved a hand at him. "Jiang Cheng! Get over here, you brat!"

Jiang Cheng scoffed. "Why? You planning to drop to your knees and thank me?"

"Seven days?!" Wei Wuxian yelled. "It took you seven days to bring help?! You were trying to get me killed!"

"Are you dead?" Jiang Cheng fired back. "Then who the hell is talking to me right now?"

"From Mount Muxi back to Yunmeng is a five-day sprint at most!"

Jiang Cheng rolled his eyes. "Are you stupid? You count the trip back, but what about the trek there? And once we got there, I had to lead a search party scouring the entire mountain for that damned banyan tree, then dig out the entrance Wen Chao and his cronies caved in! We dragged you out in seven days flat—you should be down on your knees kissing the ground!"

Wei Wuxian paused. He really had forgotten to factor in the return trip. "Oh. Fair enough, I guess. But wait, why didn't Lan Zhan point that out?"

Jiang Cheng sneered, "He was sick enough just looking at your face. You honestly think he was hanging onto your every word?"

Wei Wuxian chuckled. "Point taken!"

Jiang Yanli handed over the steaming bowl. Thick chunks of lotus root and pork ribs nestled in the broth, both stewed to a tender, pinkish perfection and piping hot, their rich aroma filling the room. After days of starving in a cave, his stomach couldn't handle heavy grease; this was the ultimate comfort food. Whispering a quick "Thanks, Shijie," he cradled the bowl and began shoveling it down, mumbling between bites, "So where's Lan Zhan? He got out too, right? Is he here, or did he go back to Gusu?"

Jiang Cheng grunted, "Obviously. He's not a Jiang; why would he come here? Of course he went back to Gusu."

"By himself? With the state of things back there..."

Before he could finish, Jiang Fengmian crossed the threshold. Wei Wuxian set his bowl down immediately. "Uncle Jiang!"

"Rest easy," Jiang Fengmian said gently. "Stay seated."

Jiang Yanli held out a handkerchief to wipe his mouth. "Is it good?"

Wei Wuxian didn't take the cloth; instead, he puckered his lips with exaggerated drama. "Delicious!"

Jiang Cheng snapped, "Don't you have hands?!"

Jiang Yanli simply chuckled, dabbing the broth from his chin and mouth before taking the empty bowl and slipping out with a happy smile. Jiang Fengmian took her vacant seat, eyeing the white porcelain crock as if hoping for a taste himself, but the bowl was already gone.

Jiang Cheng asked, "Father, is the Wen Clan still refusing to return our swords?"

Pulling his gaze back, Jiang Fengmian answered, "They are busy holding celebrations."

Wei Wuxian perked up. "Celebrating what?"

"Celebrating Wen Chao, who supposedly slayed the Xuanwu of Slaughter single-handedly."

Wei Wuxian nearly rolled clean off the cot. "The Wens took credit for the kill?!"

Jiang Cheng let out a dry, mocking laugh. "Who else? You actually expected them to announce you killed it?"

"Shameless Wen dogs!" Wei Wuxian sputtered. "Total load of crap—Lan Zhan was the one who finished it!"

Jiang Fengmian offered a faint smile. "Is that so? Funny enough, the Second Young Master of the Lan Clan told me that you were the one who killed it. So, who actually did?"

"A team effort, really," Wei Wuxian admitted. "Though he landed the killing blow. All I did was crawl inside its shell to flush it out into the open. Lan Zhan held the line outside alone, wearing it down for three grueling hours until it finally dropped."

He gave a brief rundown of their days trapped beneath the earth. Listening closely, Jiang Cheng's expression grew tangled. "Pretty much what Lan Wangji said," he muttered after a long pause. "Which means you two took it down together. Credit where credit's due—why try to pawn the whole thing off on him?"

"I'm not pawning it off," Wei Wuxian shrugged. "Compared to what he went through, I really didn't do that much."

Jiang Fengmian nodded approvingly. "You did well."

To take down a four-hundred-year-old leviathan at seventeen was leagues beyond merely 'doing well.'

Jiang Cheng crossed his arms, raising a brow. "Congratulations, then."

The congratulations carried an unmistakable edge of sour venom. Seeing him strike that prickly pose, Wei Wuxian knew his shidi's jealousy was acting up again. Jiang Cheng was undoubtedly stewing in bitter resentment, obsessing over why he hadn't been the one left behind to slay the beast, daydreaming about the glory he could have claimed.

Wei Wuxian laughed it off. "Pity you weren't there! We could've split the head three ways. At least you would've kept me entertained; sitting across from Lan Zhan for days on end nearly bored me to death."

Jiang Cheng sneered, "Serves you right. You never should've stuck your neck out in the first place, meddling in shit that didn't concern you. If you hadn't moved back then—"

"Jiang Cheng," Jiang Fengmian called out suddenly.

Jiang Cheng froze, realizing he'd crossed a line, and instantly clamped his jaw shut.

Jiang Fengmian didn't raise his voice, but the tranquil warmth had vanished from his face, replaced by a quiet, unyielding gravity. "Do you realize what was wrong with what you just said?"

Jiang Cheng hung his head. "...Yes."

Wei Wuxian tried to smooth it over. "He's just venting, Uncle Jiang, he didn't mean anything by it."

Watching Jiang Cheng's sullen, unapologetic stance, Jiang Fengmian sighed and shook his head. "A-Cheng, there are things you do not say, even in anger. To speak those words means you still fail to grasp the motto of the Yunmeng Jiang Clan. You still do not..."

"Oh, of course he doesn't grasp it! But what does that matter, so long as Wei Ying grasps it?!"

The icy, venomous interruption cut through the doorway like a crack of purple lightning. Madam Yu swept into the room on a bitter gale. Halting five paces from Wei Wuxian's cot, her brows snapped high in derision. "'Attempt the impossible'—isn't that right? Just like him, deliberately stirring up trouble even when he knows full well the disaster it will bring down upon our house!"

Jiang Fengmian frowned. "San-niangzi, what are you doing here?"

"What am I doing here? How laughable!" Madam Yu scoffed. "To think I must answer for my presence in my own home! Has Sect Leader Jiang forgotten that I am the mistress of Lotus Pier? Have you forgotten that every inch of this dirt belongs to me? Have you forgotten which one—the boy lying down, or the boy standing up—is actually your flesh and blood?!"

It was a barrage Jiang Fengmian had weathered countless times over the years. "Naturally, I remember," he replied evenly.

Madam Yu let out a chilling laugh. "You remember, but what good does remembering do? This Wei Ying—if he goes a single day without courting disaster, his skin starts itching! We should have locked him in Lotus Pier and barred him from taking a single step outside. Does Wen Chao honestly have the guts to murder the direct heirs of Gusu Lan and Lanling Jin? Even if he did, it's their rotten luck—since when was it your place to play the dashing hero?!"

Out of respect for Jiang Fengmian, Wei Wuxian kept his lips sealed, though he thought privately: Not have the guts? You clearly haven't seen that lunatic in action.

Madam Yu pointed a sharp finger toward the bed. "Mark my words: keep letting him run wild, and one of these days, he is going to drag this entire clan into ruin!"

Jiang Fengmian rose to his feet. "Let us take this conversation elsewhere."

"Take it where? Talk about what?" she snapped. "I'll say it right here! My conscience is clear. Jiang Cheng, get over here!"

Caught between his parents, Jiang Cheng hesitated for a heartbeat before shuffling over to his mother's side. Madam Yu clamped down on his shoulders, shoving him forward for Jiang Fengmian to look at. "Sect Leader Jiang, there are truths that need to be laid bare! Open your eyes and look at him! This is your biological son, the future master of Lotus Pier! Even if you despise him simply because he crawled out of my womb, his surname is still Jiang! Don't tell me you're deaf to the filthy rumors circulating out there—whispering that Sect Leader Jiang still carries a torch for a certain rogue cultivator, treating her orphan like his own child, while everyone gossips about whether Wei Ying is actually your—"

"Yu Ziyuan!" Jiang Fengmian roared.

Madam Yu raised her voice to match him beat for beat. "Jiang Fengmian! You think barking at me changes a damn thing?! As if I don't see right through you!"

The two stormed outside, trading furious barbs down the corridor. Madam Yu's venomous shrieks echoed off the courtyard walls, met by Jiang Fengmian's tightly checked fury as their argument faded into the distance.

Jiang Cheng stood frozen in place. After an agonizing silence, he cast a dark, unreadable look at Wei Wuxian, spun on his heel, and walked out.

"Jiang Cheng!" Wei Wuxian called.

Jiang Cheng ignored him, rounding the corner of the veranda at a brisk march. Wei Wuxian rolled out of bed, ignoring his sore, stiff limbs as he bolted after him. "Jiang Cheng! Hey, Jiang Cheng!"

Jiang Cheng kept his chin down and his stride furious. Losing his patience, Wei Wuxian lunged forward and locked an arm around his neck from behind. "You hear me calling, and you still walk away?! You're begging for a beating!"

"Get off me!" Jiang Cheng snarled, trying to shove him back. "Go crawl back into bed!"

"Not a chance. We're hashing this out right now! Don't you dare listen to that nonsense."

Jiang Cheng’s voice turned biting cold. "What nonsense?"

"All of it! It's so foul it dirty's a man's mouth just to repeat it," Wei Wuxian said firmly. "My parents were respectable people with proper names, and I won't have bastards muddying my lineage!"

Hooking an arm around Jiang Cheng's shoulders, he dragged him over to the wooden railing lining the covered boardwalk, forcing them both to sit. "Let's lay our cards on the table. No sulking, no bottling things up. You're Uncle Jiang's biological son and the future heir of the Jiang Clan—naturally he has to hold you to a higher standard."

Jiang Cheng cut a venomous side-eye at him.

Wei Wuxian pressed on, "I'm different. I'm someone else's kid. My parents were Uncle Jiang's close friends, so of course he treats me with extra courtesy. You understand how that works, don't you?"

Jiang Cheng sneered, "He's not holding me to a higher standard. He just doesn't like me."

"What father dislikes his own son? Stop overthinking! If I catch anyone spreading those filthy rumors, I'll beat them so hard their own mothers won't recognize them."

"He dislikes my mother," Jiang Cheng murmured, staring at the floorboards. "And by extension, he dislikes me."

That was a bitter truth Wei Wuxian couldn't refute.

The entire cultivation world knew that Madam Yu and Jiang Fengmian had grown up training alongside each other as disciples. Jiang Fengmian was gentle and refined, while Yu Ziyuan was proud, fierce, and abrasive; their paths rarely crossed, and despite matching social standing, nobody had ever considered them a couple. Later, Cangse Sanren emerged from the mountains. Passing through Yunmeng, she hit it off with Jiang Fengmian, night-hunting together on numerous occasions with deep mutual admiration. Everyone had assumed Cangse Sanren would become the next mistress of Lotus Pier.

Then, out of nowhere, the Meishan Yu Clan formally proposed a marriage alliance to the Yunmeng Jiang Clan.

The reigning Jiang Sect Leader at the time had been thrilled by the prospect, but Jiang Fengmian had resisted. Disapproving of Yu Ziyuan’s temperament, he considered them ill-suited and politely declined multiple times. Yet the Meishan Yu Clan applied immense political pressure from every angle on the young, unestablished Jiang Fengmian. Shortly after, Cangse Sanren eloped with Jiang Fengmian's most trusted retainer, Wei Changze, choosing the life of a wandering rogue. With his heart's path severed, Jiang Fengmian finally yielded.

Though husband and wife, they lived as bitter strangers, maintaining separate quarters and clashing at every exchange. Beyond reinforcing the clan's political clout, nobody knew what the marriage had actually achieved.

The founder of the Yunmeng Jiang Clan, Jiang Chi, had been an itinerant wanderer who championed a free-spirited, open-hearted, and chivalrous way of life—a spirit entirely at odds with Madam Yu’s sharp, suffocating temperament. Jiang Cheng, taking after his mother in both looks and temper, naturally failed to capture his father's favor. No matter how Jiang Fengmian tutored him, the boy couldn't bend to his ideal mold, leaving Jiang Fengmian visibly lukewarm toward his heir.

Jiang Cheng shoved Wei Wuxian's arm away, jumping to his feet as the dam broke. "I know it! I don't have the temperament he likes! I'm not the heir he wanted! He thinks I'm unfit to lead, that I don't understand the clan motto, that I lack the Jiang spirit! Fine! Be that way!"

His voice climbed, raw and frayed. "You and Lan Wangji took down the Xuanwu of Slaughter together! Covered in blood, bathing in glory! Incredible! But what about me?!"

He slammed a fist into the wooden pillar, his teeth grinding audibly. "...I ran myself ragged for days! Pure exhaustion, without a single heartbeat of rest!"

"Screw the clan motto!" Wei Wuxian barked. "Just because a motto exists doesn't mean you have to choke on it! Look at Gusu Lan—three thousand damn rules! If a man tried following every single one, how the hell is he supposed to breathe?"

He vaulted off the railing, landing in front of him. "And who says a clan leader has to be a carbon copy of his ancestors? Over the generations, do you think every Jiang Sect Leader was cut from the exact same cloth? Even the pristine Lan Clan produced an outlier like Lan Yi! Did anyone dare deny her power or standing? When scholars list the great masters of Gusu Lan, who dares skip her name? Who could ever overlook her Chord Murder technique?"

Jiang Cheng fell quiet, his breathing slowing as the fury cooled.

Wei Wuxian slung an arm around his shoulder again, his voice dropping into a warm, confident grin. "When you become Sect Leader, I'll be your right-hand man—just like your father and mine. What's so great about the Twin Jades of Gusu? Yunmeng will have the Twin Prides! So shut up. Who says you aren't fit to be clan leader? Nobody gets to say that—not even you. Try it again and I'll beat you black and blue."

Jiang Cheng scoffed, "Look at you right now. Who are you beating up?"

To prove his point, he shoved Wei Wuxian right in the chest. Though the scorched brand had been dressed and bandaged, taking an unexpected jab directly over the raw burn hurt like hell.

Wei Wuxian let out a strangled roar: "Jiang Cheng! You're dead!"

Jiang Cheng sidestepped the incoming strike, shouting back, "If it hurts that bad, why the hell did you play the hero in the first place?! Serves you right! Let that be a lesson to you!"

"I wasn't playing the hero!" Wei Wuxian yelled, clutching his chest. "My body just moved before my brain could catch up! Stop running—spare my life for a second, I need to ask you something! There was an empty medicine pouch tucked into my sash. Did you see it?"

Jiang Cheng frowned. "The one that girl Mianmian gave you? Didn't see it."

Wei Wuxian sighed, clicking his tongue. "Damn. Guess I'll have to ask her for another one next time."

Jiang Cheng grimaced. "Here we go again. You don't actually fancy her, do you? She's decent-looking, sure, but her background is completely ordinary. Probably not even an official disciple, just the daughter of a servant."

Wei Wuxian gave him a flat look. "What's wrong with servants? I'm the son of a servant too, aren't I?"

"Are you honestly comparing yourself to her?!" Jiang Cheng snapped. "What servant gets their lotus seeds hand-peeled and soup lovingly brewed by the young mistress of the house?! I didn't even get a sip of that soup!"

"If you're craving soup, just ask Shijie to make another pot," Wei Wuxian waved off. "Anyway, back to Lan Zhan. Did he leave any message for me? Did he find his brother? How are things back at his home?"

Jiang Cheng scoffed, "You expected him to leave a message? Be grateful he didn't leave a sword through your gut. He went back. Lan Xichen is still missing, and Lan Qiren has his hands completely full trying to keep the clan from falling apart."

Wei Wuxian’s brow furrowed. "And his father? How is he?"

Jiang Cheng's voice dropped.

"He passed away."
